basis: Authored teaching illustrations; no real-chart assignments

pattern.two_position_alternation.summary: Alternate between two positions: A, B, A, B.
pattern.two_position_alternation.watch: Follow the evenly spaced notes. Every next note changes to the other position.
pattern.two_position_alternation.contrast: A, A, B, B repeats positions in pairs instead of alternating on every note.
pattern.two_position_alternation.variants: The two positions and speed can change. Simultaneous notes or extra positions need a separate description.
pattern.two_position_alternation.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.same_position_repetition.watch: Each circle is a new input, even though it returns to the same place.
pattern.same_position_repetition.contrast: One long hold has a single beginning. It is not a series of repeated taps.
pattern.same_position_repetition.variants: Spacing may vary. Button repetition and touch repetition should keep their input type visible.
pattern.same_position_repetition.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.gallop_pairs.watch: Read the gaps: short, long, short, long. The pattern is in the spacing between inputs.
pattern.gallop_pairs.contrast: Evenly spaced inputs have no alternating short-long gap.
pattern.gallop_pairs.variants: Positions and the gap ratio may change. This descriptive label does not specify one musical subdivision.
pattern.gallop_pairs.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.three_note_burst.summary: Three close inputs form one short burst.
pattern.three_note_burst.watch: Longer gaps separate each group of three from the next group.
pattern.three_note_burst.contrast: A continuous stream has no larger gap marking three-note groups.
pattern.three_note_burst.variants: A three-note burst can use many rhythms. Three notes do not automatically mean triplets.
pattern.three_note_burst.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.triplet_grid.summary: Divide each beat into three equal parts.
pattern.triplet_grid.watch: Three evenly spaced inputs fit between each pair of whole-beat guide lines.
pattern.triplet_grid.contrast: Four equal inputs per beat use a four-part subdivision, even if only three happen to be visible.
pattern.triplet_grid.variants: The beat reference matters. Counting three notes alone cannot establish a triplet rhythm.
pattern.triplet_grid.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.offbeat_onsets.summary: Repeat inputs between the main beats.
pattern.offbeat_onsets.watch: These notes land halfway between the numbered beat lines.
pattern.offbeat_onsets.contrast: Notes on the numbered lines are on the beat, not the offbeat shown here.
pattern.offbeat_onsets.variants: This lesson illustrates the half-beat offbeat. Other displaced phases should be named explicitly.
pattern.offbeat_onsets.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.simultaneous_group.summary: Play two or more inputs together.
pattern.simultaneous_group.watch: Notes aligned vertically share one authored time.
pattern.simultaneous_group.contrast: A small time gap makes these successive inputs, even if they look close together.
pattern.simultaneous_group.variants: The input types and positions can vary. Visual proximity alone does not establish simultaneity.
pattern.simultaneous_group.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.chord_stream.watch: Each time column contains a pair, and the paired groups continue in sequence.
pattern.chord_stream.contrast: One simultaneous pair followed by single inputs is not a stream of paired groups.
pattern.chord_stream.variants: Group size, positions and spacing may change. No particular hand assignment is implied.
pattern.chord_stream.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.tap_staircase.summary: Step through neighboring buttons along a short arc.
pattern.tap_staircase.watch: The highlighted position moves 1 → 2 → 3 → 4, one neighboring button at a time.
pattern.tap_staircase.contrast: The 1 → 3 → 5 → 7 sequence skips buttons; it is not this neighboring-button staircase.
pattern.tap_staircase.variants: A staircase can start elsewhere or reverse its direction. A long traversal is described as a perimeter run.
pattern.tap_staircase.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.perimeter_run.summary: Progress around much of the outer button ring.
pattern.perimeter_run.watch: The sequence visits all eight buttons in ring order.
pattern.perimeter_run.contrast: Alternating between two opposite buttons does not travel around the ring.
pattern.perimeter_run.variants: Runs can cover a partial or full circuit and begin at any position. This example makes no claim about required hands.
pattern.perimeter_run.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.direction_reversal.summary: Change direction within a button run.
pattern.direction_reversal.watch: The sequence goes 1 → 2 → 3 → 4, then returns through 3 → 2 → 1.
pattern.direction_reversal.variants: The turn can occur anywhere. A jump across the ring is not enough to establish a reversed traversal.
pattern.direction_reversal.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.same_head_slide_fan.summary: One star starts multiple slide branches.
pattern.same_head_slide_fan.watch: Both paths share the same star input at button 1. The head is pressed once.
pattern.same_head_slide_fan.contrast: Two separate stars at different buttons start independent slides, not one shared-head fan.
pattern.same_head_slide_fan.variants: Branch paths and timing can differ. Count the shared physical head once.
pattern.same_head_slide_fan.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.staggered_slide_starts.summary: Start overlapping slide movements at different times.
pattern.staggered_slide_starts.watch: The second solid movement line starts while the first is still moving.
pattern.staggered_slide_starts.contrast: Both movements starting together creates overlap without staggered starts.
pattern.staggered_slide_starts.variants: Different star times do not guarantee different movement starts; compare the solid lines after each wait.
pattern.staggered_slide_starts.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.moving_slide_overlap.summary: Two or more slide paths move at once.
pattern.moving_slide_overlap.watch: The solid movement intervals overlap. Waiting paths do not count as moving.
pattern.moving_slide_overlap.contrast: The first path finishes exactly when the second starts. Their movements do not overlap.
pattern.moving_slide_overlap.variants: Head times and path shapes can vary; the defining feature is a shared interval of movement.
pattern.moving_slide_overlap.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.slide_tap_interleave.summary: Tap while another slide is moving.
pattern.slide_tap_interleave.watch: The independent tap lands inside the slide's solid movement interval.
pattern.slide_tap_interleave.contrast: A tap during the dashed waiting interval is a waiting-phase interaction instead.
pattern.slide_tap_interleave.variants: Many arrangements contain this broad interaction. It does not by itself identify Umiyuri.
pattern.slide_tap_interleave.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.delayed_slide_interleave.summary: Tap during another slide's waiting interval.
pattern.delayed_slide_interleave.watch: The tap occurs after the star input but before the solid movement line begins.
pattern.delayed_slide_interleave.contrast: This tap lands after movement starts, outside the waiting interval.
pattern.delayed_slide_interleave.variants: Wait length can vary. The slide's own head is not an independent intervening tap.
pattern.delayed_slide_interleave.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.variable_slide_wait.summary: Change the delay from star input to slide movement.
pattern.variable_slide_wait.watch: Compare the dashed waits: the first lasts one beat and the second lasts half a beat.
pattern.variable_slide_wait.contrast: These two slides have the same wait. Different travel lengths alone would not change that.
pattern.variable_slide_wait.variants: Compare waits in a stated unit. A tempo change can alter seconds without changing the wait in beats.
pattern.variable_slide_wait.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.connected_slide_chain.summary: Follow several connected segments as one slide.
pattern.connected_slide_chain.watch: One star begins the continuous route 1 → 3 → 5 → 7. The intermediate points are not new inputs.
pattern.connected_slide_chain.contrast: Three separately started slides each have their own star and wait.
pattern.connected_slide_chain.variants: Real connected segments may use different shapes or speeds. The straight segments here illustrate continuity only.
pattern.connected_slide_chain.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.hold_tap_interleave.summary: Keep one input held while other taps arrive.
pattern.hold_tap_interleave.watch: The long amber interval is active when the independent taps appear.
pattern.hold_tap_interleave.contrast: Here the hold ends before the taps start, so they do not occur during it.
pattern.hold_tap_interleave.variants: The held input can be a supported touch hold. A hold beginning is one input, not a repeated-tap stream.
pattern.hold_tap_interleave.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.hold_slide_overlap.summary: A hold stays active while a slide moves.
pattern.hold_slide_overlap.watch: The hold interval and solid slide movement share part of the timeline.
pattern.hold_slide_overlap.contrast: The hold ends at the slide's launch, so only its waiting interval overlaps the hold.
pattern.hold_slide_overlap.variants: Do not infer a required hand assignment from these intervals. Positions and geometry still matter.
pattern.hold_slide_overlap.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.touch_tap_interleave.summary: Alternate inner touch inputs with button taps.
pattern.touch_tap_interleave.watch: Square marks are touches in the inner screen area; circles are perimeter-button taps.
pattern.touch_tap_interleave.contrast: Alternating between two perimeter buttons changes position but never changes to an inner touch.
pattern.touch_tap_interleave.variants: Touch positions and order can vary. A touch at the same time as a button is a simultaneous mixed group.
pattern.touch_tap_interleave.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

pattern.umiyuri.summary: Repeat a star-and-tap pair, an intervening tap, then launch the previous slide at the next pair.
pattern.umiyuri.watch: Step through pair → intervening tap → next pair plus previous launch. The star role alternates between the two starting positions.
pattern.umiyuri.contrast: One tap during one slide lacks this recurring phase relationship.
pattern.umiyuri.variants: This lesson shows one regular form. Omitted taps, changed paths and phrase boundaries need variant-specific treatment; no compulsory hands are assigned.
pattern.umiyuri.scope: Illustration inferred from the cited explanations. It is not a song transcription or a complete definition of every Umiyuri variant.

sources.label: なめあ: first-chorus explanation
sources.note: Text and illustrated timing explanation; one scoped form.

sources.label: Surone: The Umiyuri Pattern Explained
sources.note: Retained transcript review: 3:59–7:12 and 12:03–13:45; automatic captions may contain errors.

trait.high_onset_density.summary: Many new inputs arrive in a short time.
trait.high_onset_density.watch: This example has 12 inputs per second, compared with 3 in the contrast. The vertical axes use the same scale.
trait.high_onset_density.contrast: The lower rate is less dense under this stated comparison.
trait.high_onset_density.variants: High density needs a stated threshold or reference group. Break value and ongoing movement do not add new onsets.
trait.high_onset_density.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.bursty_density.summary: Short busy bursts interrupt quieter stretches.
trait.bursty_density.watch: The isolated busy sections rise sharply above the chart's usual activity.
trait.bursty_density.contrast: An even rate has no local burst, even if its overall input count is substantial.
trait.bursty_density.variants: Bin width affects apparent burst size. A density burst is not necessarily a three-note burst.
trait.bursty_density.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.sustained_density.summary: A busy rate continues across a long stretch.
trait.sustained_density.watch: Six consecutive sections stay at 10 inputs per second. Compare this run with the isolated peak.
trait.sustained_density.contrast: One busy second followed by quieter activity is a spike rather than sustained activity.
trait.sustained_density.variants: State both the rate threshold and required duration. These values illustrate the idea, not a universal difficulty cutoff.
trait.sustained_density.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.backloaded_density.summary: More inputs arrive toward the end.
trait.backloaded_density.watch: Compare equal-length early and late sections on the same scale.
trait.backloaded_density.contrast: The contrasting activity is concentrated near the beginning instead.
trait.backloaded_density.variants: A busier ending is not necessarily a harder ending; note types and coordination can differ.
trait.backloaded_density.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.frontloaded_density.summary: More inputs arrive toward the beginning.
trait.frontloaded_density.watch: The early sections contain more new inputs per second than the later sections.
trait.frontloaded_density.contrast: The contrasting activity builds toward the end.
trait.frontloaded_density.variants: Compare sections of equal duration. This describes activity placement, not total difficulty.
trait.frontloaded_density.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.isolated_density_spike.summary: One separated busy peak stands out.
trait.isolated_density_spike.watch: One section rises clearly above the quieter sections on both sides.
trait.isolated_density_spike.contrast: Several separated peaks do not form a single isolated spike.
trait.isolated_density_spike.variants: Peak prominence and bin width must be stated when measuring real charts.
trait.isolated_density_spike.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.multi_peak_density.watch: Quieter sections separate the prominent peaks.
trait.multi_peak_density.contrast: One broad busy plateau has no quiet gaps separating multiple peaks.
trait.multi_peak_density.variants: Changing the analysis window can merge nearby peaks. The graph uses equal one-second sections.
trait.multi_peak_density.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.steady_density.summary: New inputs arrive at a fairly even rate.
trait.steady_density.watch: Each one-second section has the same number of inputs.
trait.steady_density.contrast: Large swings between busy and quiet sections are not steady activity.
trait.steady_density.variants: Even onset counts do not prove that note spacing, coordination or difficulty are constant.
trait.steady_density.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.low_onset_gaps.summary: Few new notes arrive, though ongoing actions may remain.
trait.low_onset_gaps.watch: The input rate drops in the middle. The labeled interval shows a slide still moving through that gap.
trait.low_onset_gaps.contrast: Continuing input activity provides no low-onset gap.
trait.low_onset_gaps.variants: A gap in new inputs is not automatically a rest; retain holds and slide movement separately.
trait.low_onset_gaps.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.break_concentration.summary: Break inputs cluster in particular sections.
trait.break_concentration.watch: The outlined break counts cluster in the middle; total input activity stays unchanged.
trait.break_concentration.contrast: The same total break count spread evenly across sections is less concentrated.
trait.break_concentration.variants: Break inputs are included in the total, not added to physical density. Scoring risk needs a separate interpretation.
trait.break_concentration.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.rhythm_variability.summary: The spacing between successive inputs changes.
trait.rhythm_variability.watch: Read the changing gaps along the beat grid, rather than just the total count.
trait.rhythm_variability.contrast: The same number of evenly spaced inputs has less timing variation.
trait.rhythm_variability.variants: Variation alone does not establish musical complexity. Tempo changes and chosen beat units affect the measurement.
trait.rhythm_variability.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.slide_occupancy.summary: Slide movement fills much of the timeline.
trait.slide_occupancy.watch: The labeled movement intervals cover ten of these twelve seconds. Overlap is counted once.
trait.slide_occupancy.contrast: Short movement intervals occupy much less of the same span.
trait.slide_occupancy.variants: Waiting slides are excluded. High occupancy does not identify a particular named motif.
trait.slide_occupancy.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.repeated_motif.watch: Each labeled phrase repeats the same A, B, B, A input order and timing.
trait.repeated_motif.contrast: Equal note counts with changed positions and timing do not establish the same phrase.
trait.repeated_motif.variants: A real matcher must state whether rotation, reflection or tempo changes are allowed. Shared broad tags are not enough.
trait.repeated_motif.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.

trait.isolated_pattern_sections.summary: A chosen pattern has little competing activity around it.
trait.isolated_pattern_sections.watch: The highlighted A/B alternation sits by itself. Compare the extra simultaneous inputs in the other example.
trait.isolated_pattern_sections.contrast: The same target sequence remains, but additional inputs compete with it.
trait.isolated_pattern_sections.variants: Isolation is specific to a target pattern and neighborhood. It does not by itself prove practice effectiveness.
trait.isolated_pattern_sections.scope: Authored illustration of this project's descriptive definition.
